answer: In a market where agents trade willow seedlings, each seller identity must lock $100 for 30 days before listing goods. Even if a cipher conceals common ownership, creating 10,000 sellers ties up $1 million: splitting funds among aliases cannot satisfy every bond. The attacker pays financing costs on that capital and cannot withdraw it early, even when other holdings hit their nadir. This makes mass identity creation costly without needing to identify each operator.
